criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
criteria.evidence: Purdue BuildingShapesZip4 FID 826 and both Purdue/official chapter address records identify Beta Theta Pi at 150 Littleton Street. The wall shell follows the official GIS polygon; the saved GIS/aerial overlay supports the property match.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
criteria.evidence: The project geographic transform and full GIS polygon are used without box rescaling. Evaluated asset bounds in Blender are [[805.983, 827.11], [-417.268, -375.652], [-0.12, 15.0]]. Aerial overlay supports plan placement, but the photo facade has no surveyed compass bearing and the roof/facade alignment to individual GIS edges is interpretive.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.evidence: Three facade levels now match the official front photographs, and the housing directory reports four floors plus a basement; above-grade count remains an interpretation. Roof bands and the tower are now differentiated, but the east/west/aerial views still show oversized intersecting facets, abrupt roof seams, and exposed triangular wall-top areas. The roof silhouette/pitch does not yet read like the photo's discrete slate gables. The GIS height fields remain contradictory/unusable.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
criteria.evidence: The revision adds the tall pale bay with three arched glazed levels, a separate central brick gable, and an arched stone entry with plaque, all recognizable in chapter photos 1, 11, 14, 15 and 16. Brick tone and pale stone/window trim are source-consistent. Several west/east windows still appear partly occluded by or set into roof planes, while secondary elevations use a repeated generic sash layout; exact facade bearing and openings remain unregistered to GIS.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
criteria.evidence: Fresh-open check is this independent Blender 5.2.3 process: expected scene and collection loaded; 339 collection objects/339 meshes, five materials (['Beta Theta Pi | charcoal slate roof', 'Beta Theta Pi | dark reflective window glass', 'Beta Theta Pi | painted cream window frames', 'Beta Theta Pi | pale limestone trim', 'Beta Theta Pi | warm red-brown brick']), and no missing external image paths ([]). The evidence record includes raw GIS, layer metadata, official chapter gallery and address sources, aerial overlay, source-derived decisions and uncertainties. No public interior plan is available, so the interior is correctly omitted but remains unmodeled.

findings: Rebuild the roof panels so they follow each concave GIS cross-section instead of spanning between only the global minimum and maximum X intersections; the current rendered roof still has bridged/overlapping facets and exposed wall-top triangles.
Align upper-floor windows and the pale bay/portal to the roof eaves so they remain visible and do not intersect or disappear behind the roof surfaces.
Retain the improved three-level central bay, central gable, and entry, while using additional source views to resolve roof bearings and hidden elevations.
No reliable floor plan was found; interior remains unmodeled rather than invented.
